Alright, the recent steps have gotten the project into a fairly complete state. I've just verified that a browser is installed (both Edge and Chrome returned True). That's good because the next logical step is to set up automated testing of the game in a headless browser environment. The user (or the overall task) likely wants to run the game and verify UI behavior, maybe to catch any runtime errors that static syntax checks missed.

To do that, I need a Node environment with a browser automation library. Puppeteer is the standard tool for controlling Chrome/Edge via the DevTools protocol. Since the project already uses Node (we have npm scripts, and the validation scripts run via node), I can install puppeteer-core locally in the project directory. I should avoid pulling in the full Chromium binary (which puppeteer does by default) because the user already has a real browser installed; puppeteer-core is sufficient to connect to it.

I need to run the npm commands inside the project folder (D:\project-5). First, ensure a package.json exists; `npm init -y` will create one with defaults, and I can suppress its output by redirecting to $null. Then install puppeteer-core with `npm i puppeteer-core`. I want to keep the console output manageable, so I’ll pipe errors to stdout and then select the last two lines, which typically contain the success or error summary. Also, I should disable the audit and fund messages to keep it clean (`--no-audit --no-fund`). 

Thus, the appropriate PowerShell command is:

```
cd D:\project-5; npm init -y *> $null; npm i puppeteer-core --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 2
```

This will initialize the project if not already done, install puppeteer-core, and give me a concise result. I’ll use the PowerShell tool to execute this command, with a description indicating that I'm installing puppeteer-core for browser testing.
